summary: Magnesium supports muscle and nerve function and contributes to protein, bone and DNA production.

functions.title: Physiological role
functions.description: Magnesium supports muscle and nerve function and contributes to protein, bone and DNA production.

functions.title: Food context
functions.description: Legumes, nuts, seeds, whole grains and leafy vegetables provide magnesium.

referenceValues.notes: FDA label reference for adults and children aged 4+. Not a personalised target, EAR, RDA or UL.

foodSourceRules.notes: Comparable source-backed composition per 100 g; not a health score or a measure of individual absorption.

absorptionFactors.description: Different supplement salts can differ in absorption; a food-composition amount does not measure how much a person absorbs.

deficiency.overview: Sustained low intake or conditions affecting absorption and losses can lead to magnesium deficiency; short-term low intake may have no obvious symptoms.
deficiency.medicalBoundary: Symptoms are nonspecific and cannot diagnose a nutrient deficiency. Diagnosis may require clinical evaluation and appropriate laboratory testing.

excess.overview: High supplemental or medicinal magnesium can cause diarrhoea and cramping; extremely high intake can disrupt heart rhythm. The supplemental upper limit excludes magnesium naturally present in food.
excess.medicalBoundary: An upper limit is not an intake goal. Seek medical or professional advice before changing supplement or medication use.
